protocol.name: beize_app_v1

description.summary: what every app of Beize may ask (ADR 0028)

protocol.description: What AppKit hands to the WindowServer: a material below a surface, and its menus, which the shell shows in the menu bar. Every client is offered it; the compositor keeps an app's glass inside its own surface. Both ends live in Beize's repository and change together: until a version of Beize promises otherwise, the protocol grows without new versions.

interface.name: beize_glass_manager_v1

description.summary: glass below surfaces, and the appearance that tints it

interface.description: On bind the compositor tells the appearance.

event.name: appearance
event.description: The system's appearance, and again when it changes: glass is tinted by it, so what an app draws on glass follows it.

request.name: get_glass
request.description: Glass below part of a panel's surface or of a popup: base glass, the background blurred once, until set otherwise (ADR 0028 §6). Its shapes are double-buffered state of the surface: they apply with the surface's next commit. One per surface; it may lie in several places (add_shape), as the control center's tiles. A toplevel gets none.

interface.name: beize_glass_v1
interface.description: Until a shape is set, there is none. Destroying the object takes the glass away with the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_shape
request.description: A rectangle in the surface's coordinates with round corners of radius (the continuous corners of Beize's shader), and whether a rim of light runs along its edge (1) or not (0).

entry.name: base
entry.summary: the background, blurred once: costs next to nothing

entry.name: live
entry.summary: what lies behind it, windows too, blurred when it changes

entry.name: menu
entry.summary: live glass tinted thickly, as macOS' menus: calm, what lies behind barely shows

entry.name: clear
entry.summary: liquid glass, its tone held so white ink reads on it: the control center's

entry.name: liquid
entry.summary: liquid glass without ink on it: the dock's

request.name: set_material

description.summary: base, live, menu, clear or liquid glass

request.description: Base glass until set otherwise (ADR 0028 §6). Double-buffered as the shape.

request.name: add_shape
request.description: Glass in one more place, as set_shape describes, besides those set before (set_shape starts again with one). Of the same material, and each with a shadow if the glass has one.

request.name: set_shadow
request.description: Whether the compositor draws a soft shadow around each of its shapes (1) or not (0), as macOS' WindowServer gives menus one. None until set. Double-buffered as the shape.

request.name: set_smoke

description.summary: what lies around the glass, blurred

request.description: Whether what lies behind the glass's shapes and around them is blurred too, beyond the surface: from each shape's edge outwards, less and less over falloff px, by strength px (the Gaussian's standard deviation) at most – a smoke that keeps what lies behind from showing sharp between the shapes. It lies behind the panel too, and takes no input. A falloff or strength of 0: none, as until set. Double-buffered as the shape.

description.summary: an app's menus for the menu bar

request.name: get_menu
request.description: Of the xdg_toplevel with the surface, shown in the menu bar while the window is active. One per window.

interface.name: beize_app_menu_v1
interface.description: Described anew whole, between begin and commit: what comes in between applies at commit. Limited in number and length by the compositor, which drops what lies beyond.

description.summary: a menu after the last, by its title

request.name: add_item

description.summary: a command at the end of the last menu

request.description: Activated by its id, the app's. The shortcut is only shown; empty: none. The app handles its keys itself.

description.summary: a line at the end of the last menu
the window has no menus any more
